specification.title: A transactional migration's reversal deletes its marker and then fails
steps: Revert. m1's reversal deletes its marker and then raises an error. The migration is transactional, so the deletion is in the reversal's transaction.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the revert has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: If a migration's reversal fails, the operation reports failure and the migration's history entry remains; for a transactional migration, its marker also remains.

execution.description: TypeORM's defaults, with the managed transaction API ds.transaction(callback).
execution.form: DataSource.runMigrations() and DataSource.undoLastMigration(), migrationsTableName migrations. The migration object is built for the case. Its name ends in a 13-digit timestamp, which MigrationExecutor.getMigrations() requires.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on x86_64-pc-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

knowledge: A reported failure says the revert did not complete. For a transactional migration, the caller can treat the migration as still applied.

api_outcome.contract: TypeORM 1.1.2 DataSource.runMigrations() executes pending migrations and undoLastMigration() reverts the last one (data-source/DataSource.js). MigrationExecutor defaults to transaction mode "all": one transaction wraps every pending migration, and the history insert is inside it (migration/MigrationExecutor.js). There is no advisory lock.

error.message: the reversal failed on purpose after deleting the marker
